b: Stacy Keach, an actor who could move from Shakespeare to stoner comedy without making it seem like he was slumming, has died at his home in Magdalenka, Poland. He was 85. His wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach, announced the death in a statement, saying that he passed away after “a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure.”

Born in Savannah, Georgia, in 1941, Keach trained at Yale and, on a Fulbright, at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art, and he spent much of the 1960s and ’70s as one of the New York stage’s most formidable classical actors. He played Falstaff and Hamlet for Joseph Papp at the Delacorte, earned a Tony nomination for playing Buffalo Bill in the Broadway production of Arthur Kopit’s Indians, and kept returning to the big roles for decades, from King Lear in Chicago and Washington to Richard Nixon in the touring production of Frost/Nixon.

On screen, his defining performance came early: As Billy Tully, the washed-up boxer drinking his way into oblivion in Fat City, he gave John Huston’s 1972 film its battered, rueful heart. He followed it with Richard Fleischer’s The New Centurions, played a hapless narc in the Cheech and Chong stoner classic Up in Smoke, and starred as Frank James opposite his brother James’s Jesse in Walter Hill’s The Long Riders, which he also co-wrote and executive produced.

Television made him a household name as Mickey Spillane’s Mike Hammer in the 1980s, and he won a Golden Globe for the 1988 miniseries Hemingway. His later film work included John Carpenter’s Escape from L.A., Tony Kaye’s American History X, and Alexander Payne’s Nebraska, and his final screen appearance came in Noah Baumbach’s Jay Kelly.
